questions.text:
Bag $\mathrm{B}_{1}$ contains 6 white and 4 blue balls, Bag $\mathrm{B}_{2}$ contains 4 white and 6 blue balls, and Bag $\mathrm{B}_{3}$ contains 5 white and 5 blue balls. One of the bags is selected at random and a ball is drawn from it. If the ball is white, then the probability, that the ball is drawn from Bag $\mathrm{B}_{2}$, is :
(1) $\frac{1}{3}$
(2) $\frac{4}{15}$
(3) $\frac{2}{3}$
(4) $\frac{2}{5}$

steps:
$\mathrm{E}_{1}$ : Bag $\mathrm{B}_{1}$ is selected
$$\begin{array}{lll}
B_{1} & B_{2} & B_{3} \\
\text { 6W 4B } & \text { 4W 6B } & \text { 5W 5B }
\end{array}$$
$\mathrm{E}_{2}$ : bag $\mathrm{B}_{2}$ is selected
$\mathrm{E}_{3}$ : Bag $\mathrm{B}_{3}$ is selected
A : Drawn ball is white
We have to find $\mathrm{P}\left(\frac{\mathrm{E}_{2}}{\mathrm{~A}}\right)$
$$\begin{array}{l}
P\left(\frac{E_{2}}{A}\right)=\frac{P\left(E_{2}\right) P\left(\frac{A}{E_{2}}\right)}{P\left(E_{1}\right) P\left(\frac{A}{E_{1}}\right)+P\left(E_{2}\right) P\left(\frac{A}{E_{2}}\right)+P\left(E_{3}\right) P\left(\frac{A}{E_{3}}\right)} \\
=\frac{\frac{1}{3} \times \frac{4}{10}}{\frac{1}{3} \times \frac{6}{10}+\frac{1}{3} \times \frac{4}{10}+\frac{1}{3} \times \frac{5}{10}} \\
=\frac{4}{15}
\end{array}$$

questions.text:
Let $\mathrm{f}: \mathrm{R} \rightarrow \mathrm{R}$ be a twice differentiable function such that $f(2)=1$. If $\mathrm{F}(\mathrm{x})=\mathrm{x} f(\mathrm{x})$ for all $\mathrm{x} \in \mathrm{R}$, $\int_{0}^{2} x F^{\prime}(x) d x=6$ and $\int_{0}^{2} x^{2} F^{\prime \prime}(x) d x=40$, then $\mathrm{F}^{\prime}(2)+\int_{0}^{2} \mathrm{~F}(\mathrm{x}) \mathrm{dx}$ is equal to :
(1) 11
(2) 15
(3) 9
(4)

steps:
$$\begin{array}{l}
\int_{0}^{2} x F^{\prime}(x) d x=6 \\
=\left.x F(x)\right|_{0} ^{2}-\int_{0}^{2} f(x) d x=6 \\
=2 F(2)-\int_{0}^{2} x F(x) d x=6[\therefore f(2)=2 F(2)=2] \\
\int_{0}^{2} x F(x) d x=-2 \\
\Rightarrow \int_{0}^{2} F(x) d x=-2
\end{array}$$

Also
$$\begin{array}{l}
\int_{0}^{2} x^{2} F^{\prime \prime}(x) d x=\left.x^{2} F^{\prime}(x)\right|_{0} ^{2}-2 \int_{0}^{2} x F^{\prime}(x) d x=40 \\
=4 F^{\prime}(2)-2 \times 6=40 \\
F^{\prime}(2)=13 \\
\therefore F^{\prime}(2)+\int_{0}^{2} F(x)=13-2=11
\end{array}$$

questions.text:
A bar magnet has total length $2 l=20$ units and the field point P is at a distance $\mathrm{d}=10$ units from the centre of the magnet. If the relative uncertainty of length measurement is 1\%, then uncertainty of the magnetic field at point P is :
(1) 10\%
(2) 4\%
(3) 3\%
(4) 5\%

steps:
Method-1 :
Without considering uncentainity in $\ell$.
$$\begin{array}{l}
\mathrm{B}=\frac{\mu_{0}}{4 \pi} \frac{\mathrm{~m}}{\mathrm{r}^{3}} \\
\mathrm{~B} \propto \frac{1}{\mathrm{r}^{3}} \\
\frac{\Delta \mathrm{~B}}{\mathrm{~B}}=3 \times\left(\frac{\Delta \mathrm{r}}{\mathrm{r}}\right)
\end{array}$$
\% uncertainity in $\mathrm{B}=3 \%$
Method-2 :
With considering uncentainity in $\ell$.
$$\begin{array}{l}
\mathrm{B} \propto \frac{1}{\mathrm{r}^{3}} \\
\frac{\Delta \mathrm{~B}}{\mathrm{~B}}=\frac{\Delta \ell}{\ell}+3 \times\left(\frac{\Delta \mathrm{r}}{\mathrm{r}}\right)=1+3 \times 1=4 \%
\end{array}$$
\% uncertainity in $\mathrm{B}=4 \%$
